Exercise 9.2 — When CPO is TRPO, and a second CPO step by hand
      
      
        Consider the CPO subproblem $\max_xg^{	op}x$ s.t. $c+b^{	op}x\le0$, $	frac12x^{	op}Hx\le\delta$ with $H\succ0$, $\delta\gt0$ and $g
e0$ (so $q=g^{	op}H^{-1}g\gt0$). (a) Derive its dual function $D(\lambda,
u)=\max_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda,
u)$ for $\lambda\gt0$, $
u\ge0$, and show that $D$ is jointly convex. (b) Show that if the TRPO step satisfies the linearised constraint, $c+r\sqrt{2\delta/q}\le0$, then $(\lambda,
u)=(\sqrt{q/(2\delta)},0)$ minimises $D$, so CPO returns the TRPO step (the claim in the theorem of Section 3). (c) Take $g=(1,\,0.4)$, $b=(0.6,\,0.8)$, $H= egin{pmatrix}2&0.5\0.5&1\end{pmatrix}$, $\delta=0.05$, $c=-0.1$, and use $H^{-1}g=(0.457,\,0.171)$, $H^{-1}b=(0.114,\,0.743)$. Compute $q,r,s$, decide the regime, compute $\lambda^\star,
u^\star,x^\star$, and verify strong duality numerically.
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) $\mathcal L=g^{	op}x-
u(c+b^{	op}x)-\lambda(	frac12x^{	op}Hx-\delta)$ is strictly concave in $x$ for $\lambda\gt0$; $
abla_x\mathcal L=g-
u b-\lambda Hx=0$ gives $x= rac1\lambda H^{-1}(g-
u b)$, and substituting, $D(\lambda,
u)= rac{1}{2\lambda}(g-
u b)^{	op}H^{-1}(g-
u b)-
u c+\lambda\delta= rac{q-2
u r+
u^2s}{2\lambda}-
u c+\lambda\delta$. With $w=H^{-1/2}(g-
u b)$, affine in $
u$, the first term is $\|w\|^2/(2\lambda)$, the perspective of the convex function $	frac12\|w\|^2$; perspectives are jointly convex in $(w,\lambda)$ on $\lambda\gt0$, and composing with an affine map preserves convexity. The other two terms are linear.
            (b) Let $\lambda_0=\sqrt{q/(2\delta)}\gt0$. Multiplying the hypothesis by $\lambda_0$ gives $\lambda_0c+r\le0$. First-order conditions of the convex problem $\min_{\lambda\gt0,
u\ge0}D$ at $(\lambda_0,0)$: $\partial_\lambda D=- rac{q}{2\lambda_0^2}+\delta=0$, and $\partial_
u D= rac{
u s-r}{\lambda}-c=- rac{\lambda_0c+r}{\lambda_0}\ge0$, the correct sign for a minimiser on the boundary $
u=0$. For a convex differentiable function these conditions are sufficient, so $(\lambda_0,0)$ is a global minimiser, and Step 4 of the walkthrough maps it to $x^\star=H^{-1}g/\lambda_0=\sqrt{2\delta/q}\,H^{-1}g=x_{m TRPO}$, with value $D=\sqrt{2q\delta}=g^{	op}x_{m TRPO}$.
            (c) $q=0.457+0.4\cdot0.171=0.526$, $r=0.114+0.4\cdot0.743=0.411$, $s=0.6\cdot0.114+0.8\cdot0.743=0.663$. $c^2/s=0.0151\le2\delta=0.1$: the hyperplane cuts the trust region. TRPO test: $c+r\sqrt{2\delta/q}=-0.1+0.411\cdot0.436=+0.079\gt0$, so (b) does not apply and $
u^\star\gt0$. $\lambda_a=\sqrt{ rac{q-r^2/s}{2\delta-c^2/s}}=\sqrt{ rac{0.2703}{0.0849}}=1.784$, inside $\Lambda_a=[0,\,r/|c|)=[0,\,4.11)$; $
u^\star= rac{\lambda_ac+r}{s}= rac{-0.178+0.411}{0.663}=0.352$; $x^\star= rac{1}{1.784} ig[(0.457,0.171)-0.352\,(0.114,0.743) ig]=(0.234,\,-0.050)$. Checks: $c+b^{	op}x^\star=-0.1+0.140-0.040=0$ and $	frac12x^{\star	op}Hx^\star=0.050=\delta$ (both active); $g^{	op}x^\star=0.234-0.020=0.214$. Dual value: $D_a(\lambda_a)=\sqrt{(q-r^2/s)(2\delta-c^2/s)}- rac{rc}{s}=0.152+0.062=0.214$: zero duality gap. For comparison, $D_b$ at its projected minimiser $\lambda_b=\max ig(\sqrt{q/(2\delta)},\,r/|c| ig)=\max(2.29,4.11)=4.11$ is $ rac{q}{2\lambda_b}+\lambda_b\delta=0.064+0.206=0.270\gt0.214$, which confirms $\lambda^\star=\lambda_a$ (the $\Lambda_a$ case of regime 2). Enter these values in the explorer (with $H_{12}=0.5$, $H_{22}=1$) to see the step.
